records.rationale: The diff shows `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}` in group.hbs rendering group_member.hbs, whose template reads `{{#unless automatic}}` to gate the remove link. records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:90 — remove_member` calls `group.users.delete(user_id)` (which mutates the join table immediately) and then calls `group.save`, which does nothing for the removal and misleadingly implies the delete is not yet persisted
records.rationale: The diff shows `group.users.delete(user_id)` in remove_member; in Rails a has_many association .delete destroys the join record immediately, so the subsequent `group.save` is redundant for the removal and its failure path (`render_json_error(group)`) could return a 422 after the deletion already persisted. Not a defect in the happy path (deletion still works), but a concrete API-semantics/code-correctness concern grounded in this diff.

records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — limit` param has no upper bound, allowing a client to request an arbitrarily large page of group members (minor DoS/resource use)
records.rationale: The diff line `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` in app/controllers/groups_controller.rb indeed accepts a client-supplied limit with no clamping/upper bound, and this endpoint is now applied to all groups (previously the param only affected automatic groups with a 200 default), so an unbounded page size and full `group.users.count` per request is a plausible minor resource-exhaustion vector introduced here. The finding is factually accurate about the code shown, though the severity is minor and the impact cannot be fully verified from the diff alone.
